validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE test applied: MAP test (the scope-mandated test for this cohort, since P80xx rows were identified visually off the GASCO national-grid map on printed p.35 of EGAS Annual Report 2018 -- a full-text miss there is NOT dispositive per the scope note). I rendered that map at high resolution (locally cached at batches/egypt-gas/archive/staging/route-creation-20260807/maps/egas2018_p35_gasco_national_grid.png) and traced the Suez/Gulf corridor by hand. A green (existing) line runs from the 'Sokhna' distribution-center icon (Ain Sokhna) north along the Gulf coast, past 'Ayoun Moussa', to a node explicitly labeled 'Abu Soultan P.S.' -- i.e. exactly this row's route -- carrying the label '24" - 145 km'. This corroborates EXISTENCE and the NAMING/ENDPOINTS (Ain Sokhna, Suez governorate -> Abu Sultan, Ismailia governorate is correct) but see the SPEC concern below: the label's own numbers do not match the sheet.

TEXT test: ran a full pdftotext -layout extraction of the complete 40-page EGAS Annual Report 2018 (cached at /Users/baird/Dropbox/_gem-docs/mapping/2026-gas/egypt-2026/EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf). 'Sokhna'/'Sukhna' does not appear anywhere in the report's running text -- consistent with this being a map-only (visual) citation, exactly the pattern the scope note describes for this cohort, not evidence the citation is bad.

INDEPENDENT-SOURCE cross-check (two comprehensive trunk-line inventories, found via a sibling row's research this batch): Egypt Oil & Gas Newspaper Sept 2020 Issue 165 p.13 ('Gulf of Suez, Eastern Desert and Sinai') tables all SEVEN Gulf-of-Suez/Sinai gas trunk lines by name (Trans Gulf Gas; Zaafarana-Korimat; Zeit Bay-Ras Shukheir; Ras Shukheir-Suez Gas Trunkline; Suez-Cairo Ring; Suez-Port Said; El Arish Gas Pipeline) -- no 'Ain Sokhna-Abu Sultan' line appears in that list. The separate egyptoil-gas.com feature 'Egypt's Gas Distribution Network, An Intricate Economic Web' (Wood Mackenzie-sourced), which enumerates the Nile-Delta/Cairo/Nile-Valley trunk group by name, also does not mention Sokhna or Abu Sultan. So existence rests on the map alone -- single-sourced, not independently corroborated -- which is why this validity item is 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than a clean pass, and why tier is low despite no existence doubt.

DUPLICATE check against the roster, specifically the Abu-Sultan-hub cluster: P8002 (El Tina-Abu Sultan-New Administrative Capital, Abu Sultan->Cairo, 73 km, 42in) approaches Abu Sultan from the NORTH (El Tina/Sinai coast) and continues WEST to Cairo/NAC -- a different corridor and diameter. P8036 (Mit Nama-Abu Sultan P.S., Mit Nama->Ismailia, 114 km, 16in) approaches from the WEST (Mit Nama, near Cairo). P8074 (Abu Sultan-El Shabab, Abu Sultan->Ismailia, 38 km, 24in) continues NORTHEAST from Abu Sultan. P8033 is the SOUTH approach into the same hub, from Ain Sokhna on the Gulf of Suez. All four are geometrically distinct legs converging on/radiating from one real pressure-station hub (Abu Sultan P.S., confirmed on the map itself) -- not duplicates or relabels of each other. Classification ('transmission') is consistent with a national-grid trunk feeding a named pressure station and is not separately flagged.

validity.recommendation: Re-derive Length and Diameter from the map crop before trusting the sheet's current 106.00 km / 32 in -- the map's own label for this exact corridor reads 24" - 145 km. Correct LengthKnown to ~145.00 km and Diameter to 24 in (source: the map on p.35 of the already-cited EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF), or at minimum escalate for a human to compare the map crop directly, since this is the ONLY source found for the row and it conflicts with the sheet. Separately: flag scripts/url_verifier.py's PDF handling -- see tooling-defect note below -- since the 'expected content present' passes it produced for this row's Length/Diameter units are false positives, not real corroboration, and the same defect likely affects other map/PDF-sourced units in this cohort.
validity.researcher_notes:
SPEC check, applying the corroboration rule strictly ('a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline'): the map at batches/egypt-gas/archive/staging/route-creation-20260807/maps/egas2018_p35_gasco_national_grid.png labels the Ain-Sokhna-to-Abu-Soultan-P.S. line '24" - 145 km' (verified at 5x crop zoom, unambiguous digits, not confusable with e.g. '34' or '29'). GEM currently records LengthKnown=106.00 km and Diameter=32 in for this row. Both numbers disagree materially: length is 27% short of the map's 145 km, and diameter is one full nominal size off (24in vs 32in) -- this is exactly the 'material disagreement' the corroboration rule requires flagging, not silently passing, even though the disagreement is against the row's OWN best/only source rather than a second independent one.

WHY the sheet's ref checks look clean when they should not: existing_ref_checks for this row's Length and Diameter units both report '200 + expected content present' against the current [ref] (the EGAS 2018 PDF). I ran the SAME url_verifier.py logic and confirmed it: verify_url(...,'106') on this URL returns OK/'expected content present'. But a full pdftotext -layout extraction of the complete PDF (1108 lines) contains NO occurrence of the digits '106' anywhere, and NO occurrence of '32"' anywhere near a Sokhna/Sultan context (the one '32"' in the whole document is an unrelated 'New Capital / Dahshur Pipeline 70 km - 32"' entry). Reading url_verifier.py's source confirms why: it has no PDF-text-extraction step at all -- `body = r.text` decodes the RAW PDF bytes (this file is a heavily image/DCTDecode-compressed PDF, confirmed via a separate fetch attempt that could not read its content either) as if they were plain text, then does a lowercase substring search over that binary-garbage decode. A short numeric needle like '106' or '32' can coincidentally appear inside compressed/binary byte noise -- this is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a real content match, and it is a distinct failure mode from the documented 'large PDF, extractor doesn't reach the whole doc' caveat already in the script's docstring (that caveat describes false NEGATIVES on big text-based PDFs; this is a false POSITIVE on an image-based one). This is a tooling defect, not something to route through the routine ref-quality flag -- I'm surfacing it here because it directly produced unwarranted confidence in this row's now-disputed numbers, but fixing/re-running the checker tracker-wide is outside a single-PID audit's scope.

Only one source exists for this corridor at all (the map), so I cannot independently cross-check 145 km / 24in against a second origin -- tier is low and this is flagged as a concern for human adjudication rather than an outright value replacement.

summary: P8033 Ain Sokhna-Abu Sultan: existence/naming/duplicate all confirmed (caveat: single-sourced to the GASCO map, no independent second source names this corridor) -- but the map's OWN label for this exact line reads 24"-145km, materially disagreeing with the sheet's 32in/106.00km, and the automated ref-checks that appeared to confirm those sheet numbers are false positives (url_verifier has no real PDF-text extraction and matched digit noise in a compressed/image PDF, confirmed via manual pdftotext). Recommend correcting Length/Diameter (or escalating to a human to compare the map crop) rather than trusting the current values. No UNRESOLVED fills.
